resources.string: Burkan is tested only on the Galaxy S23, S23+ and S23 Ultra. It may not work on this phone.
You type the pairing code into a notification, and Burkan reports on its runs there.
In Settings, open About phone › Software information and tap Build number seven times.
In Developer options, switch on Wireless debugging and tick “Always allow on this network”.
In Wireless debugging, tap “Pair device with pairing code”. Then pull down the notification shade and type the six-digit code into Burkan’s notification.
Waiting for the code in the notification.
Burkan connects to wireless debugging on this phone.
Burkan grants itself the permission to switch wireless debugging, so it can work after a restart without you.
Let Burkan run after a restart
Without this, battery optimisation may stop Burkan from applying Vulkan when the phone starts.
This screen is not built yet.
Wireless debugging needs Wi-Fi. Connect to a Wi-Fi network and try again.
Wireless debugging is off. Switch it on in Developer options.
The phone switched wireless debugging straight back off. Turn it on once by hand on this Wi-Fi network and tick “Always allow on this network”.
Wireless debugging did not answer. Check that it is on, then try again.
The phone no longer accepts Burkan’s pairing. Pair again.
Burkan could not connect to wireless debugging. Try again.
The connection to wireless debugging was lost. Try again.
The phone took too long to answer. Try again.
The pairing code is six digits.
The pairing dialog is closed. Tap “Pair device with pairing code” again, then reply with the new code.
That code did not match. Check the code in the pairing dialog and reply again.
Pairing timed out. Start it again.
Burkan could not give itself the permission it needs. Try again.
Where you type the pairing code from Wireless debugging.
In Wireless debugging, tap “Pair device with pairing code”, then reply here with the six-digit code.
Return to Burkan to finish setup.
